pumac-2018-algebra-b-01.title: Solve for |x-25|
pumac-2018-algebra-b-01.body:
Take reciprocals: $1+\dfrac{1}{|x-25|}=\dfrac{50}{49}$, so $\dfrac1{|x-25|}=\dfrac1{49}$ and $|x-25|=49$.

Hence $x=25+49=74$ or $x=25-49=-24$, and the sum is $74+(-24)=50$.

**Answer: 50**

pumac-2018-algebra-b-01.title: Symmetry
pumac-2018-algebra-b-01.body:
The equation depends only on $|x-25|$, so its solutions come in pairs symmetric about $25$: $x=25\pm t$. Solving $\frac{t}{t+1}=\frac{49}{50}$ gives $50t=49t+49$, $t=49$. The two solutions add to $2\cdot 25=50$.

**Answer: 50**

pumac-2018-algebra-b-02.title: Telescoping
pumac-2018-algebra-b-02.body:
Each term is $\dfrac1{m(m+3)}=\dfrac13\left(\dfrac1m-\dfrac1{m+3}\right)$, so the sum telescopes:
$$\frac13\left(\frac12-\frac1{n+3}\right)=\frac{25}{154}.$$
Then $\frac12-\frac1{n+3}=\frac{75}{154}$, so $\frac1{n+3}=\frac{77-75}{154}=\frac{1}{77}$ and $n=74$.

**Answer: 74**

pumac-2018-algebra-b-02.title: Count the terms
pumac-2018-algebra-b-02.body:
Write the denominators as $(3k-1)(3k+2)$ for $k=1,2,\dots$; the last one is $n=3k-1$. By telescoping, the sum of the first $k$ terms is $\frac13\left(\frac12-\frac1{3k+2}\right)=\frac{k}{2(3k+2)}$. Setting $\frac{k}{2(3k+2)}=\frac{25}{154}$ gives $154k=150k+100$, so $k=25$ and $n=3\cdot25-1=74$.

**Answer: 74**

pumac-2018-algebra-b-03.title: Geometric series
pumac-2018-algebra-b-03.body:
The first $1$ is in decimal place $k$ and the second in place $2k$, so $a_k=10^{-k}+10^{-2k}$. Then
$$\sum_{k\ge1}a_k=\sum_{k\ge1}10^{-k}+\sum_{k\ge1}100^{-k}=\frac19+\frac1{99}=\frac{11+1}{99}=\frac4{33}.$$
So $p+q=4+33=37$.

**Answer: 37**

pumac-2018-algebra-b-04.title: Find a_n
pumac-2018-algebra-b-04.body:
Multiply by $n^2$: $\sum_{k=1}^n k^2a_k=n^2$. Subtracting the same identity for $n-1$ gives $n^2a_n=n^2-(n-1)^2=2n-1$ (also true for $n=1$), so
$$a_n=\frac{2n-1}{n^2}=1-\left(1-\frac1n\right)^2,$$
which is decreasing in $n$.

Now $a_n<\frac1{2018}\iff 2018(2n-1)<n^2\iff n^2-4036n+2018>0$. At $n=4036$ the left side is $2018>0$; at $n=4035$ it is $2018-4035<0$. Since $a_n$ is decreasing, the smallest such $n$ is $4036$.

**Answer: 4036**

pumac-2018-algebra-b-05.title: The sequence has period 5
pumac-2018-algebra-b-05.body:
Compute: $x_2=\frac{1+x_1}{x_0}$, $x_3=\frac{1+x_0+x_1}{x_0x_1}$, $x_4=\frac{1+x_0}{x_1}$, $x_5=x_0$, $x_6=x_1$. So the sequence has period $5$, and $x_{2018}=x_3$ since $2018\equiv3\pmod5$.

Set $\dfrac{x_0+x_1+1}{x_0x_1}=\dfrac1{1000}$, i.e. $x_0x_1-1000x_0-1000x_1=1000$, i.e.
$$(x_0-1000)(x_1-1000)=1000^2+1000=1000\cdot1001=2^3\cdot5^3\cdot7\cdot11\cdot13.$$
Both factors have the same sign. Two negative factors would each exceed $-1000$ in absolute value, so the product would be less than $10^6<1001000$: impossible. So both are positive divisors, and $x_0-1000$ can be any divisor of $1001000$, which fixes $x_1$. The number of divisors is $4\cdot4\cdot2\cdot2\cdot2=128$ (every such choice gives positive $x_0,x_1$).

**Answer: 128**

pumac-2018-algebra-b-06.title: Factor and use QM-AM
pumac-2018-algebra-b-06.body:
$ab+bc+cd+da=(a+c)(b+d)$. Let $r=a+c$, $s=b+d$: $r+s=17$, $rs=46$, so $r^2+s^2=17^2-2\cdot46=197$ (and $r,s$ are real, being roots of $t^2-17t+46$ with discriminant $105>0$).

Since $a^2+c^2\ge\frac{(a+c)^2}2$ and $b^2+d^2\ge\frac{(b+d)^2}2$,
$$a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2\ge\frac{r^2+s^2}{2}=\frac{197}2,$$
with equality when $a=c=r/2$, $b=d=s/2$. So the minimum is $\frac{197}2$ and $p+q=199$.

**Answer: 199**

pumac-2018-algebra-b-07.title: Complete the square
pumac-2018-algebra-b-07.body:
Let $T=\sum_{i=0}^9\epsilon_i2^i$. The double sum is over all pairs $j<i$, so
$$\sum_{j<i}\epsilon_i\epsilon_j2^{i+j}=\frac12\left(T^2-\sum_{i=0}^{9}4^i\right)=\frac12\left(T^2-\frac{4^{10}-1}{3}\right)=\frac12\left(T^2-349525\right).$$
$T$ is odd (only $\epsilon_0\cdot 1$ is odd), so $T^2\ge1$, and $T=\pm1$ is attainable: $\epsilon_9=+1$ and all others $-1$ gives $512-511=1$. Hence $m=\frac12(1-349525)=-174762$.

**Answer: 174762**

pumac-2018-algebra-b-08.title: Cotangent substitution
pumac-2018-algebra-b-08.body:
Multiplying the condition by $abc$ gives $1+bc+ab=ac$, so $b=\dfrac{ac-1}{a+c}$. Put $a=\cot x$, $c=\cot y$; then $b=\cot(x+y)$ by the addition formula. Since $\frac1{\cot^2t+1}=\sin^2t$, the expression is
$$4\sin^2x+4\sin^2(x+y)+7\sin^2y=4-2\cos2x-2\cos(2x+2y)+7\sin^2y.$$
Using $\cos2x+\cos(2x+2y)=2\cos(2x+y)\cos y$ and $\sin^2y=1-\cos^2y$, with $u=\cos y$ and $w=\cos(2x+y)\in[-1,1]$:
$$=11-7u^2-4uw\le 11-7u^2+4|u|.$$
The right side is maximal at $|u|=\frac27$, where it equals $11-\frac47+\frac87=\frac{81}7$. This is attained: take $\cos y=\frac27$ and $2x+y=\pi$, so $a=\tan\frac y2$, $b=-\tan\frac y2$, $c=\cot y$ are all non-zero. Thus $M=\frac{81}7$ and the answer is $81+7=88$.

**Answer: 88**
